pr.title: fix(github): drop the merge method when a merge queue refuses it
pr.body:
Merging a stacked review into a branch with a merge queue failed outright: the queue governs the async
endpoint a stacked pull request must use, so GitHub rejects the `stk.mergeStrategy` sent with it as an
unsupported custom parameter - and does it as a `failed` status on a `200`, which read as a failed merge.

The strategy is dropped and the merge re-sent when GitHub refuses it, which is exactly when the queue's own
configured method decides the merge anyway. Reactive rather than probing for a queue first: a probe that
answered wrong the other way would drop the method on a repo that does honour it and land the review by the
repo's default instead of the configured strategy. `merge` names the review the queue took over rather than
switching methods silently.

<!-- git-stk:closes -->
Closes #333
<!-- /git-stk:closes -->

expected.description: The merge-method refusal is only caught in the PUT response, but GitHub can report it later as a failed status at a poll, so the retry without the method never happens and the merge still fails.
